source_reviews.independent_solution: For ordinary homogeneous isotropic transparent media, incident ray, refracted ray and local normal are coplanar. With angles to the normal, n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r). For nonnormal transmission sin(i)/sin(r) = n2/n1; at normal incidence i = r = 0, the quotient is 0/0 but the product law remains valid. Collinear ray/normal do not define a unique incidence plane. These results were persisted before reading either draft.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Absolute index nj = c/vj uses vacuum as reference for the same frequency. The index of medium 2 relative to medium 1 is n21 = n2/n1 = v1/v2; reversing the pair reciprocates it. Relative index equals n2 only for reference index n1 = 1. A sine quotient is unnecessary and undefined at normal incidence.

coverage.evidence: n77-index-reference requires the vacuum/medium-pair distinction and correct ordered ratio together. Its stem defines notation without giving the ratios. Unaided comparison and derivation are declared losses; fixed frequency avoids an unresolved dispersion comparison.

source_reviews.independent_solution: For n1 > n2, r = 90 degrees gives sin(ic) = n2/n1, hence ic = arcsin(n2/n1), measured from the normal. Below ic there is transmission; equality is the boundary-parallel limiting direction; above ic there is total internal reflection. No sub-grazing TIR critical angle exists for incidence from n1 <= n2.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A paraxial bundle incident parallel to the principal axis of a converging lens actually meets at its outgoing real principal focus. For a diverging lens, only backward extensions of outgoing rays meet at its incident-side virtual principal focus. Opposite illumination defines the other focus; equal surrounding media give equal focal-distance magnitudes. The focus is not the center or every finite object's image.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Under the seed's thin-lens, paraxial, equal-medium, real-positive convention, 1/d + 1/f = 1/F. F = 10, d = 5 gives f = -10; F = -10, d = -5 gives f = +10, so lens type alone does not universally determine image reality.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Linear magnification is corresponding image-size magnitude divided by object-size magnitude, Gamma = image/object = |f|/|d|, nonnegative and dimensionless. It does not encode upright/inverted orientation. With d = 30, f = 60 the ratio is +2, not -2 or 1/2; squaring gives area scaling, not linear magnification. The draft defines H as object and h as image, so its size ratio is h/H.
